title: Refusing to be polished into something else
odia: ମୋତେ ଯେତେ ମାଠିବୁ ମାଠ ମୁହିଁ ସେଇ ଦରପୋଡ଼ା କାଠ
literal_meaning: Polish me as much as you like; I remain that half-burnt wood.
explanation: The speaker declares that repeated efforts to change or improve them will not work. The blunt material image can make the refusal comic, defiant or self-deprecating. It voices a stance in a conversation, not a truth that people cannot learn or change.
meaning_odia: ଘଷିଲେ ବି ଅବସ୍ଥା ବଦଳିବ ନାହିଁ—ଏମିତି ଏକ ଜିଦ୍ ବା ନିଜକୁ ନେଇ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀର ସ୍ୱର ଏଠାରେ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ଅଧାପୋଡ଼ା କାଠର ଉପମାରେ ଅନ୍ୟର ବଦଳାଇବା ଚେଷ୍ଟାକୁ ଅଗ୍ରାହ୍ୟ କରିବାର ଭାବ ଆସେ। ଏହା ମଣିଷ ବଦଳିପାରେନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ।
usage_example: After repeated advice to adopt a more fashionable manner, someone jokingly insists that they will remain as they are. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The wood image and the first-person voice are preserved. This is distinct from enduring pressure: here the emphasis falls on resisting another person’s attempts to remake the speaker. The half-burnt wood supplies an image of stubborn resistance, not proof that people cannot change.

english_summary: The speaker defiantly refuses to change; the saying voices a stance, not a limit on learning.
